text:
Rajat (SI-Northstar): quick heads-up — Northstar customer hitting failures pulling our marketplace private image inside their air-gapped VPC. Errors: 'unauthorized: authentication required' and 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' on some nodes. They have an outbound proxy and strict egress rules. Need exact registry endpoints, IP allowlist, and CA guidance.

Maya (Partnerships): Thanks — looping in infra and solutions. @Keiko any registry/ports details we can share ASAP? @Jon can help with proxy/containerd guidance.

Keiko (Eng-Infra): Registry hostname: gcr.redwood-inference.com (443). We publish marketplace from these IPs: 34.56.78.90/32 and 35.66.77.88/32 (customer should allow outbound 443 to those).
Also common gotchas: install our CA into the node/container runtime so image pulls trust the cert. Example for containerd/docker: 
```
sudo mkdir -p /etc/docker/certs.d/gcr.redwood-inference.com
sudo cp redwood-root.crt /etc/docker/certs.d/gcr.redwood-inference.com/ca.crt
sudo systemctl restart containerd
```

Jon (Solutions): If their proxy terminates TLS (MITM), the runtime needs the proxy's CA in the same place. Also ensure proxy supports HTTP CONNECT for TLS to registry. If containerd sits behind a corporate proxy, add `HTTP_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` on node and in systemd drop-ins.

Rajat (SI-Northstar): They say they installed the root cert at OS level but containerd still fails. Logs: `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`. Example command we ran: `docker pull gcr.redwood-inference.com/northstar/rlm:1.2.0` -> unauthorized.

Keiko (Eng-Infra): For the `unauthorized` part, confirm image visibility and whether imagePullSecrets are configured. If their nodes cannot reach our token endpoint for auth, pulls will 401. For troubleshooting we can temporarily open a short window to make the image public.

Liam (Customer Success): Customer asking for a quick architecture call tomorrow 09:00 PST to unblock implementation — can we do 30m?

Maya (Partnerships): I can do 09:00 PST. @Keiko are you available? @Jon too?

Keiko (Eng-Infra): :thumbsup: I can make 30m. Also recommend adding a short allowlist for the customer's NAT IPs to our registry; easier than changing their proxy. We can also provide a signed cert for their proxy if they want.

Rajat (SI-Northstar): Sharing debug snippets we captured:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect gcr.redwood-inference.com:443 -showcerts
...certificate chain shows Redwood Root CA as issuer...
```
and
```
$ docker pull gcr.redwood-inference.com/northstar/rlm:1.2.0
Error response from daemon: unauthorized: authentication required
```

deploy-bot: private-image-release: image northstar/rlm:1.2.0 temporarily set to public for troubleshooting window 2026-04-05T16:00Z - 2026-04-05T18:00Z by release-team (will revert).

Jon (Solutions): If we go that route, make sure to provide the customer with a sample imagePullSecret and a note to remove public access after. Sample: 
```
kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=gcr.redwood-inference.com \
  --docker-username=_json_key --docker-password='${JSON_KEY}' --docker-email=ops@northstar.example
```
Also check their `containerd` certs dir, e.g. `/etc/containerd/certs.d/` and systemd env for proxy.

Rajat (SI-Northstar): I'll confirm customer accepts the public window and send them the secret sample + the containerd cert install steps. Scheduling 09:00 PST arch call now.

Liam (Customer Success): Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Customer will try the public window and we have the call scheduled. :pray:
